proxy_language: Proto-Saharan (Nilo-Saharan, Saharan branch: Kanuri, Teda-Daza, Zaghawa-Beria), with a Berber/Tamasheq-style layer as a secondary, speculative alternative
proxy_rationale: The Early Acacus (c. 10200-8000 BP, Tadrart Acacus, SW Libya) left no linguistic record. Nilo-Saharan (Saharan branch) is a defensible, though highly debated, proxy for Holocene Central Saharan hunter-gatherers (Blench; Bender). Berber (Afroasiatic) is the main competing candidate, but most scholars date its Saharan spread later (pastoral/Garamantian/Late Holocene). Proto-Saharan, reconstructed by Jakobi, Lukas and Cyffer, is the best available proto-language. The link between the archaeological culture and any language is unproven, so all names are plausible-sounding rather than attested.
phonology: Proto-Saharan consonants (Cyffer/Jakobi style): stops *p *b *t *d *k *g, affricates *c *j (tS dZ), fricatives *s *z *h, nasals *m *n *ny *ng, liquids *l *r, glides *w *y. Vowels *i *e *a *o *u, with length contrast in modern descendants. Kanuri adds implosive-like and retroflex-ish allophones, with a prenasalized series (mb, nd, ng, nj). Tone is present in Kanuri and Teda-Daza but not marked in standard orthography.
phonotactics: Predominantly open or CVC syllables: (C)V(C), with CVC the common root shape. Root forms are usually CVC, CVCV or CVCVC. Consonant clusters occur only across syllable boundaries, often nasal+stop (mb, nd, ng, nj) or liquid+stop. Words rarely begin with a cluster and rarely begin with a vowel. Final consonants are typically sonorants or simple stops (n, r, l, m, k, t). No aspirated stops, so digraphs like th, ph, bh, dh and kh are not native.
orthography: Practical Latin transliteration in the style of Kanuri/Teda grammars: c = [tS], j = [dZ], sh = [S], ny = [J], ng = [N], w, y as glides, vowels a e i o u, long vowels doubled (aa, ee) if needed, '*' prefix for reconstructed forms. No diacritics are required. Aspirates and the th/ph/kh/bh/dh digraphs should be avoided.
morphology: Agglutinative, predominantly suffixing. Roots are largely monosyllabic or disyllabic. Nouns take plural suffixes (Kanuri -ya, -wa, Teda -a), case or relational suffixes (genitive -ye/-be in Kanuri), and a definite/determiner suffix (-ro, -ben). Verbs take extensive suffixing for tense/aspect. Reduplication is used for intensity, plurality and iterativity. There is no noun-class prefix system as in Niger-Congo.
compounding: Compounds are head-final: modifier + head (Kanuri kadai 'goat-kid' type, Teda ko-kinna). Genitive constructions are possessor + possessum, linked by a genitive linker or direct juxtaposition: [owner]-ye [possessed]. Agent nouns use verb root + -ma/-ba (agentive, e.g. Kanuri -ma 'person of'). Place names add suffixes such as -ri / -ni (locative). Descriptive names combine a noun with an adjective or a quality root: [noun][adj].
noun_phrase_order: Head-final within the NP: Possessor + Noun; Noun + Adjective (adjective follows noun in Kanuri); Determiner/demonstrative follows the noun; Numeral follows the noun. For game names: [Modifier][Head] compounds, optionally [Possessor]-genitive [Head].

attested_roots.gloss: to see/eye-related (Saharan eye root, cf. Kanuri nyim, Teda mi)
water/river (Teda/Zaghawa reflexes, Saharan water root, uncertain)

worked_examples.name: Banduri

worked_examples.name: Bandoni
worked_examples.gloss: ba 'water' + ndo 'open land' + -ni locative: 'open-land of water'

worked_examples.name: Nyimlanye
worked_examples.gloss: nyim 'eye' + lan 'hill' + -ye genitive: head follows possessor in a juxtaposed order

notes: All names must be understood as speculative: no language is known for the Early Acacus culture. Avoid the aspirated and digraph-heavy shapes in the current game names (Bhuxi, Dhose, Thandini, Yibuph, Khuphi). No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word, since the language is not Goidelic. Note that the pattern for final consonants is deliberately restrictive; the final-letter forbidden pattern can be relaxed to allow final vowels (a, e, i, o, u), sonorants and k. Prefer names built from the 10-16 roots plus -ri, -ni, -ye suffixes.
